pr_title: feat: Add SQL support for `GROUP BY ALL` syntax and fix several issues with aliased group keys
pr_body:
Closes #15585 (ref: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/14704#issuecomment-2048020360)

## Feature

`GROUP BY ALL` is a useful SQL construct (as implemented by BigQuery, DuckDB, Snowflake, etc) that allows for automatic grouping by column expressions in the SELECT clause that are not (and do not contain) aggregate/window functions.

```python
from datetime import date
import polars as pl

dt1 = date(1999, 12, 31)
dt2 = date(2028, 7, 5)

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "key": ["xx", "yy", "xx", "yy", "xx", "xx"],
    "dt": [dt1, dt1, dt1, dt2, dt2, dt2],
    "value": [10.5, -5.5, 20.5, 8.0, -3.0, 5.0],
})

df.sql(
    """
    SELECT dt, key, SUM(value) AS total,
    FROM self
    GROUP BY ALL
    ORDER BY dt, key
    """
)
# shape: (4, 3)
# ┌────────────┬─────┬───────┐
# │ dt         ┆ key ┆ total │
# │ ---        ┆ --- ┆ ---   │
# │ date       ┆ str ┆ f64   │
# ╞════════════╪═════╪═══════╡
# │ 1999-12-31 ┆ xx  ┆ 31.0  │
# │ 1999-12-31 ┆ yy  ┆ -5.5  │
# │ 2028-07-05 ┆ xx  ┆ 2.0   │
# │ 2028-07-05 ┆ yy  ┆ 8.0   │
# └────────────┴─────┴───────┘
```

## Fixes

* While implementing this I came across several errors with group-key aliasing/tracking, resolved them, and added test coverage. I'm aware of one more similar gremlin, but it's very much an edge-case and I'll address it in a subsequent PR.
* Use of `ARRAY_AGG` in conjunction with `GROUP BY` could result in a double-implode, due to our implicit array aggregation on bare `agg` columns in the regular API.
* Attempting to group by ordinal values should have raised on negative integers - and now it does.

issue_context.title: Add GROUP BY ALL to the SQL engine
issue_context.body:
### Description

a few SQL based databases / data warehouses support a GROUP BY ALL statement , which groups by all columns except aggregated columns (sum, etc)

this can speed up EDA work and can be a nice addition for Polars 

Examples 

BigQuery
https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax#group_by_all

DuckDB
https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/query_syntax/groupby.html

Snowflake
https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/constructs/group-by

based on discussion here https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/14704

review_comments:
L727 `let schema_before = lf.schema()?;`

Is problematic. It is very expensive on large dags as we do a complete conversion to IR to compute the schema. It also means we cannot resolve SQL server side.

Have to think of this a bit, but  maybe we should see if we can change our abstraction from `LazyFrame` to `IR` and build those.
Now the types align we can clone the `Arc` which is much cheaper.

2. That means to be able to assign owned expression we create below. `Expr` instead of `&Expr`, we must ensure we store an owned `Expr` to which we can assign (overwrite) our new Owned variants. Therefore I move the `clone` here (instead of L757 when we push).

Now we can assign our owned variants.
1. This iterates over a `&[Expr]` slice, thus you get a `&Expr` on every iteration. E.g. we borrow this expression from somewhere (the slice).
Driveby.  Use `ColumnName: Arc<str>` here. That ensures we don't allocate strings down the road and the datatypes between different ways of referring to columns align.
`HashSet` should be preferred over `BTreeSet`. It will typically be faster.
